content.text: This is a standard FRQ-style method: compute each row's sum with a nested traversal, track the maximum and its index, and use a strict greater-than comparison to preserve the smallest-index tie rule. It needs about 2 loops and 1 accumulator reset, with no tricky arithmetic and little reading. The only real pitfalls are initializing the max correctly (negative values are possible) and resetting the row sum per row. This fits typical full-mock FRQ difficulty for skill 2.A.

content.text: This is a standard 2D array algorithm in which a student writes a method that allocates a result array with swapped dimensions (grid[0].length by grid.length) and fills it with a nested loop. The reasoning steps are few: determine the new dimensions, loop over rows and columns, and assign result[c][r] = grid[r][c]. The one subtlety is the non-square case, where swapping the dimensions correctly matters. The stimulus is short, the computation is trivial, and the item stays within the unit 4 scope. It matches a typical AP free-response style item that suits full mock exams, so exam_prep fits better than basic_learning. It is not an advanced supplement because it has no tricky aliasing, no recursion, and no unusual constraints.
